title: Crisis & Integrity: The Final Challenge
description: The CAPSTONE challenge of your entire learning journey. You have been chosen to lead your school through a devastating triple crisis — a natural disaster, an ethical scandal, and a fracturing community. Every skill you have built over three years — financial thinking, negotiation, leadership, storytelling, critical thinking, AI tools, marketing, and ethical reasoning — will be tested. This is the ultimate trial of integrated soft skills. Will you rise to the challenge?
how_to_play: You lead your school through 12 critical weeks of overlapping crises.
Each round presents high-stakes decisions with cascading consequences across 5 interconnected subsystems.
Manage resources carefully — leadership, ethics, trust, finances, and communication all interact.
NPCs (Principal Torres, an investigative reporter, a community elder, and the student body) will react to your choices and may trigger additional crises.
Random events — disasters, misinformation, outside help — will force you to adapt in real time.
Some choices are locked behind resource thresholds. Build the right foundations to unlock advanced options.
Crisis events trigger when your metrics drop dangerously low. Prevent them or manage the fallout.
There are 6 possible endings — your decisions across all 12 weeks determine your legacy.
learning_objectives: Integrate all soft skills learned across the curriculum into unified decision-making
Navigate ethical dilemmas under extreme pressure and resource constraints
Lead diverse teams through crisis with empathy, communication, and strategic thinking
Balance short-term crisis response with long-term community rebuilding
Demonstrate resilience by adapting strategy when facing cascading failures
Practice transparent communication with multiple stakeholders simultaneously
Build trust through integrity even when shortcuts are available
cultural_context: School leadership during multi-layered crisis, community resilience, ethical governance, globally relevant scenarios

behaviors.message: I'm impressed by how you're handling this. The board is noticing your leadership.
We need stronger leadership right now. The school board is considering bringing in someone else.
Principal Torres calls an emergency ethics review. 'Our integrity is everything. If we lose that, we lose the school.'
Principal Torres addresses the school: 'Your crisis leader has shown us what true leadership looks like — competent and principled.'
Riya writes a balanced article: 'Student leader demonstrates remarkable transparency in crisis.'
Riya publishes a critical piece: 'School crisis deepens as leadership falters. Parents demand answers.'
BREAKING: Riya Kapoor publishes an explosive exposé: 'School Leadership in Crisis — Integrity Questions Mount.' The story goes national.
Mr. Anand tells the community: 'This young leader reminds me why we should trust the next generation.'
Mr. Anand shakes his head: 'The community is losing faith. Words without action mean nothing.'
Mr. Anand calls an emergency community meeting: 'We built this school on values. If the leadership has lost its moral compass, the community must step in.'
The student council organizes peer support groups. 'We're all in this together — that's what makes our school special.'

simulation_config.ai_scene_prompt_template: A school in crisis — leadership score {leadership_score}%, ethical standing {ethical_standing}%, community trust {community_trust}%, crisis response capability {crisis_response}%. The building shows signs of recent storm damage being repaired. Students, teachers, and community members are gathered in various states of concern and determination. Mood: {'hopeful and united' if community_trust > 60 else 'tense and divided' if community_trust < 30 else 'cautiously working together'}. Semi-realistic style.

rounds.situation: A devastating storm has torn through the area overnight. The school's east wing is flooded, the gymnasium roof has partially collapsed, and three families in the school community have lost their homes. At the same time, an alarming rumor is circulating — someone claims that emergency funds set aside last year were already spent on unauthorized purchases. The school board has appointed you as Crisis Response Leader. Every eye is on you.
rounds.goal: Establish your initial crisis response and set the tone for your leadership.
rounds.coaching_moment: First impressions in crisis define everything. How you respond in the first 24 hours shapes whether people follow you or abandon you. This is about strategic thinking AND empathy simultaneously.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What matters more in the first moments of a crisis — action or communication? Can you do both?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: School building with storm damage, flooded hallway, concerned students and teachers gathered outside, emergency vehicles, dramatic sky clearing, community members arriving, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. Establish Emergency Command Center
choices.description: Set up a structured crisis response operation — assign roles, create communication chains, assess damage systematically before acting.
choices.feedback: Excellent crisis leadership. By creating structure in chaos, you've given everyone a clear role and a sense of control. This is exactly how professional emergency managers operate.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.
skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.

choices.label: B. Rush to Help Displaced Families First
choices.description: Drop everything and personally lead the effort to help the three displaced families. Set up temporary shelter in the school's undamaged areas.
choices.feedback: Your compassion is inspiring and genuine. The families and community see that you care about people over procedures. However, without a systematic plan, other problems may escalate while you focus here.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Thinking about what's fair for everyone involved shows ethical awareness.
skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.

choices.label: C. Immediately Address the Financial Rumors
choices.description: Call an emergency assembly. Publicly acknowledge the rumor, pledge full transparency, and announce an immediate audit of all school finances.
choices.feedback: Bold and principled. Addressing rumors head-on shows integrity and courage. But with buildings damaged and families displaced, some feel the timing is wrong — physical safety first, they say.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Choosing what's right over what's easy shows moral courage.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.

choices.label: D. Split the Team — Tackle Everything at Once
choices.description: Divide your team into three groups: one handles physical damage, one helps families, one investigates the financial rumor. You coordinate from the center.
choices.feedback: Ambitious and comprehensive, but risky. Spreading your small team across three fronts means each effort is diluted. Your team is stretched thin and some are already showing strain.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Not always playing it safe helps you grow as a decision-maker.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.

rounds.situation: The initial chaos has subsided slightly, but challenges are mounting. You need a reliable team to manage this crisis long-term. Several people have stepped forward to help, but each comes with strengths, complications, and personal agendas. A senior teacher, Ms. Devi, has the most experience but clashes with younger staff. Aarav, a tech-savvy student leader, wants to use social media for coordination but has no crisis experience. A parent volunteer, Mr. Rahman, has corporate crisis management experience but some teachers distrust 'outsiders' making school decisions.
rounds.goal: Assemble your crisis leadership team and establish working dynamics.
rounds.coaching_moment: Great leaders build diverse teams. The question is not who is most qualified on paper — it is who will work together effectively under pressure. This tests your people skills.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Is it better to have the most skilled team or the most cohesive team? What happens when those are different?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Diverse group of people around a table in a school meeting room, whiteboards with crisis plans, some people standing with arms crossed, others engaged, tension and determination, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. Include Everyone — Build a Big Coalition
choices.description: Invite Ms. Devi, Aarav, Mr. Rahman, AND two student representatives. Create a large, inclusive crisis committee with clear sub-roles for each person.
choices.feedback: Inclusive and democratic — you've ensured every voice is represented. But large committees can be slow to decide and hard to coordinate under time pressure.

skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.

choices.label: B. Lean Expert Team — Ms. Devi + Mr. Rahman
choices.description: Pick the two most experienced people. Ms. Devi knows the school inside out, Mr. Rahman knows crisis management. Speed and expertise over representation.
choices.feedback: Fast and competent. This team can make decisions quickly. But students and younger staff feel excluded — and resentment builds in crises.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Evaluating risk vs. reward is a key life skill.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Prioritizing long-term gains over short-term comfort builds character.

choices.label: C. Empower Youth — Aarav Leads Digital Response
choices.description: Put Aarav in charge of a student-led digital coordination team. Use social media, messaging apps, and real-time dashboards. Ms. Devi advises but students lead.
choices.feedback: Innovative and empowering! The digital approach is modern and fast. But some parents and older staff wonder if teenagers should be running crisis communications.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.
skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.

choices.label: D. Rotating Leadership — Each Person Leads One Day
choices.description: An unconventional approach: each team member takes turns being crisis lead for a day. Everyone experiences both leading and following.
choices.feedback: A fascinating experiment in shared leadership. Everyone gains perspective by walking in others' shoes. But in a real crisis, the lack of consistent direction creates confusion.

skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.
skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.

rounds.situation: The financial audit you initiated has uncovered something troubling. The missing emergency funds were used by a beloved, long-serving teacher to secretly pay medical bills for three students whose families could not afford treatment. The teacher broke protocol and falsified expense reports — but did it to save children's health. The investigative reporter, Riya Kapoor, has caught wind of this and wants a statement. The community is watching.
rounds.goal: Decide how to handle a teacher who broke rules for compassionate reasons.
rounds.coaching_moment: This is the heart of ethical reasoning: when doing the 'right thing' and following the rules collide. There is no easy answer. Every option carries a cost — the test is whether you can reason through the tradeoffs honestly.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Can breaking rules ever be the right thing? How do you hold people accountable while also showing compassion?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: School office scene, open financial documents on desk, elderly teacher looking worried but dignified, young crisis leader facing a difficult decision, window showing reporters outside, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. Full Transparency — Public Disclosure
choices.description: Reveal everything publicly. Acknowledge the teacher's compassion but insist that rule-breaking cannot be excused. Announce new financial controls and let the community decide the teacher's fate.
choices.feedback: Radically transparent. This builds long-term institutional integrity, but the beloved teacher may suffer publicly. Some see this as principled; others see it as cold.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Considering fairness in your decision demonstrates ethical thinking.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.

choices.label: B. Compassionate Justice — Private Resolution
choices.description: Handle it privately. Reprimand the teacher internally, create a proper hardship fund for student medical needs, and tell the reporter that the matter is being resolved through internal processes.
choices.feedback: A balanced approach that honors both compassion and accountability. Creating the hardship fund addresses the root cause. But the reporter may feel you're hiding something.

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Weighing the ethical implications shows principled reasoning.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.

choices.label: C. Defend the Teacher Publicly
choices.description: Go on record defending the teacher's actions as morally justified. Challenge the system that forced a teacher to break rules to help sick children. Make it a public stand for compassion over bureaucracy.
choices.feedback: A passionate moral stand that wins hearts. But by defending rule-breaking, you weaken institutional trust. What happens when the next person breaks rules for less noble reasons?

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.
skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.

choices.label: D. Appoint an Independent Review Committee
choices.description: Neither condemn nor defend. Bring in a respected neutral party — Mr. Anand the community elder, a parent representative, and a teacher — to investigate and recommend action. You step back from the decision.
choices.feedback: A wise, democratic approach that shares the burden of a difficult decision. But some see it as avoiding responsibility — leaders are supposed to decide, not delegate the hard calls.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Standing by your values even under pressure builds integrity.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Investing effort now for later payoff builds discipline.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.

rounds.situation: Money is running out. The school's insurance covers only 40% of the storm damage. You have limited financial resources left and five competing urgent needs: rebuilding the gymnasium, restoring the computer lab, funding temporary housing for displaced families, hiring a counselor for traumatized students, and paying for the financial audit. You cannot fund everything. Every choice means something else goes unfunded.
rounds.goal: Allocate scarce resources across competing critical needs.
rounds.coaching_moment: Resource allocation under constraint is one of the hardest leadership skills. There is no right answer — only trade-offs. The key is being explicit about WHY you prioritize what you do.
rounds.reflection_prompt: When you cannot help everyone, how do you decide who to help first? What principles guide your choices?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: School leader at desk with budget spreadsheets, calculator, worried expression, multiple request forms stacked up, damaged building visible through window, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. People First — Counselor + Housing
choices.description: Prioritize human needs. Fund the mental health counselor and temporary housing for displaced families. The buildings can wait; people cannot.
choices.feedback: Deeply compassionate. Students and families feel supported and cared for. But the damaged gym and computer lab remain unusable, affecting daily school operations.

skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Thinking about what's fair for everyone involved shows ethical awareness.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Resisting the quick fix in favor of lasting results shows maturity.

choices.label: B. Infrastructure First — Gym + Computer Lab
choices.description: Rebuild the facilities that serve all 500 students daily. The gym is the only large gathering space, and the computer lab is essential for learning. Individual families will need to find other support.
choices.feedback: Pragmatic and utilitarian — you're helping the greatest number of students. But the displaced families feel abandoned, and critics call it heartless.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Waiting for the right moment instead of rushing shows self-control.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Not always playing it safe helps you grow as a decision-maker.

choices.label: C. Launch Emergency Fundraising Campaign
choices.description: Instead of choosing, find more money. Launch an aggressive community and online fundraising campaign. Use Aarav's social media skills. Takes time but could fund everything.
choices.feedback: Creative and resourceful! You're refusing to accept the false choice. The fundraising brings in money AND builds community ownership. But while you fundraise, the immediate needs remain unmet.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Evaluating risk vs. reward is a key life skill.

choices.label: D. Partial Funding for Everything
choices.description: Spread the money thin — give partial funding to all five needs. Nothing gets fully resolved, but nothing is completely ignored either.
choices.feedback: Equitable but ineffective. By funding everything partially, nothing gets properly fixed. Sometimes leadership means making hard choices rather than avoiding them.

skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.

rounds.situation: The crisis is now public. Parents are flooding the school with angry calls. Social media is a mix of support and vicious criticism. Riya Kapoor has published two articles — one fair, one harsh. A parent group is organizing a protest. Meanwhile, your team is exhausted from working around the clock. You need a communication strategy that manages public perception without dishonesty.
rounds.goal: Develop and execute a communication strategy for multiple stakeholders simultaneously.
rounds.coaching_moment: Communication under crisis is not about spin — it is about trust. Transparency builds long-term credibility even when the short-term news is bad. But HOW you communicate matters as much as WHAT you say.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Is there a difference between managing perception and being manipulative? Where is the line?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: School leader recording a video message, phone showing social media comments both positive and negative, whiteboard with communication plan, tired team in background, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. Radical Transparency — Daily Public Updates
choices.description: Create a daily crisis update channel — video updates, open Q&A sessions, real-time dashboard of recovery progress. Hide nothing, even when the news is bad.
choices.feedback: Courageous and credibility-building. People respect the honesty, even when the updates are grim. However, your team is spending significant time on communication rather than actual crisis work.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Choosing what's right over what's easy shows moral courage.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.
skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.

choices.label: B. Strategic Messaging — Controlled and Professional
choices.description: Hire a parent volunteer who works in PR. Issue polished weekly updates, carefully framed to emphasize progress. Control the narrative without lying.
choices.feedback: Professional and effective at managing perception. But 'controlled messaging' can feel corporate and inauthentic. Some parents sense they're not getting the full picture.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Prioritizing long-term gains over short-term comfort builds character.

choices.label: C. Town Hall — Face the Community Directly
choices.description: Organize a large community town hall meeting. Face parents, students, and press in person. Let them ask anything. Show you have nothing to hide.
choices.feedback: Brave and deeply personal. Facing an angry crowd takes real courage. The community respects your willingness to stand before them, even if not every answer satisfies.

skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.

choices.label: D. Let Students Tell the Story
choices.description: Train a student journalism team to document the crisis and recovery from the student perspective. Authentic voices, real stories. Let the community see through the students' eyes.
choices.feedback: Brilliant and innovative. Student voices carry authenticity that no press release can match. But you're putting young people in the media spotlight during a stressful time — is that fair to them?

skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.
skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.

rounds.situation: The physical crisis is stabilizing, but the community is fractured. Parents are divided — some support your leadership, others want you replaced. Teachers are tired and some are talking about transferring to other schools. The displaced families are still in temporary housing. Mr. Anand, the community elder, offers to help mediate but warns: 'You cannot rebuild walls if the people behind them are broken.' A local business owner offers a large donation — but with strings attached: naming rights and influence over the school's curriculum.
rounds.goal: Rebuild community cohesion and navigate a morally complex offer of help.
rounds.coaching_moment: Real community building requires patience, humility, and the willingness to listen more than you speak. The donation dilemma tests whether you can separate 'needed help' from 'compromised integrity.'
rounds.reflection_prompt: When someone offers help with conditions attached, how do you evaluate whether to accept? What is the price of integrity?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Community gathering at school grounds, people in small groups talking, some conflict visible, elder mediating, business person with briefcase watching from side, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. Accept the Donation with Conditions
choices.description: Take the money. The school desperately needs it. Naming rights are cosmetic, and you can negotiate to limit curriculum influence. Pragmatism over purism.
choices.feedback: The money helps, but the cost is high. Parents learn about the curriculum influence clause and are furious. Mr. Anand is deeply disappointed. 'You sold the school's independence for a quick fix.'

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.

choices.label: B. Reject Conditions, Counter-Propose Partnership
choices.description: Thank the business owner but reject the conditions. Counter-propose a transparent partnership: the donation is acknowledged publicly, the business gets positive coverage, but zero influence on curriculum. Take it or leave it.
choices.feedback: Masterful negotiation that protects integrity while still securing some funding. The business owner accepts the reduced terms, impressed by your principled stance. Mr. Anand nods approvingly.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Considering fairness in your decision demonstrates ethical thinking.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Not always playing it safe helps you grow as a decision-maker.

choices.label: C. Reject Donation — Community Funds Itself
choices.description: Reject the donation entirely. Instead, organize a community-wide fundraiser — every family contributes what they can, teachers volunteer time, students run events. 'We rebuild together or not at all.'
choices.feedback: Inspiring! The community rallies together with remarkable generosity. The fundraiser raises less money but generates something worth more — shared ownership and renewed bonds.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Weighing the ethical implications shows principled reasoning.

choices.label: D. Ask Mr. Anand to Lead Community Healing Sessions
choices.description: Before thinking about money, focus on healing the divisions. Mr. Anand leads a series of community circles where everyone — parents, teachers, students — shares their fears and hopes. Defer the donation decision.
choices.feedback: Deep and meaningful. The healing sessions are emotional and transformative. People who were enemies last week are sharing meals. But the donation question remains unresolved and the financial pressure grows.

skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.
skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.

rounds.situation: Riya Kapoor's latest article has gone regional. A national education magazine wants to profile your school's crisis response — either as a cautionary tale or an inspiring story, depending on what they find. Meanwhile, social media misinformation is escalating: a doctored photo shows you supposedly laughing while families lost their homes (it was actually taken at a different event months ago). The student council wants to fight back online. The parent group that opposed you is now citing the fake photo in their complaints to the school board.
rounds.goal: Handle media scrutiny and combat misinformation without losing credibility.
rounds.coaching_moment: In the age of social media, misinformation travels faster than truth. The instinct is to fight fire with fire — but responding emotionally to lies often amplifies them. This requires patience, evidence, and strategic restraint.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How do you fight lies without becoming a liar yourself? When is silence stronger than a response?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Split scene: one side showing a school leader calmly gathering evidence, other side showing angry social media posts and fake news, phones displaying viral misinformation, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. Methodical Evidence-Based Response
choices.description: Collect timestamped evidence proving the photo is fake. Create a clear, factual rebuttal document. Share it with the school board, parents, and media. Let facts speak.
choices.feedback: Precise and devastating. The evidence is irrefutable. The fake photo is debunked and the parent group loses credibility. Riya Kapoor even writes about your 'textbook response to misinformation.'

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Standing by your values even under pressure builds integrity.
skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.

choices.label: B. Student-Led Truth Campaign
choices.description: Let the student council create a social media counter-campaign — student testimonials, behind-the-scenes photos, daily video diaries showing the real story of recovery.
choices.feedback: Authentic and powerful. The student voices resonate far more than any official statement could. The national magazine notices and shifts toward an inspiring profile. But putting students in the spotlight during a crisis raises welfare concerns.

skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.
skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Evaluating risk vs. reward is a key life skill.

choices.label: C. Open-Door Policy — Invite the Magazine In
choices.description: Invite the national magazine for full, unrestricted access. Let them see everything — the damage, the recovery, the conflicts, the teamwork. Bet on the truth being compelling enough.
choices.feedback: An enormous gamble that pays off — if your house is in order. The magazine sees genuine, imperfect leadership and writes a nuanced but ultimately positive profile. Your transparency becomes the story.

skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Taking a calculated risk shows you can handle uncertainty.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Thinking about what's fair for everyone involved shows ethical awareness.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.

choices.label: D. Ignore the Noise — Focus on the Work
choices.description: Stop reading social media. Stop tracking articles. Tell your team to focus 100% on crisis recovery. The work will speak louder than any press release.
choices.feedback: Stoic and focused. Your team's morale improves without the distraction of media warfare. But the misinformation goes unchecked and the false narrative hardens in the public mind.

skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Investing effort now for later payoff builds discipline.

rounds.situation: A second crisis hits. A confidential student welfare report lands on your desk: one of your most helpful crisis team members — Priya, a student volunteer — is being bullied severely by a group that resents her visibility. She has asked you NOT to intervene because she fears it will make things worse. At the same time, a teacher privately tells you that another student is spreading the misinformation about you — and that student's parent is the leader of the protest group. You could quietly use this information to discredit the protest. No one would know.
rounds.goal: Navigate two morally complex situations that test your integrity when no one is watching.
rounds.coaching_moment: This is the ultimate ethical test: what do you do when no one would know? When you have power over someone who is trying to harm you? And when helping someone might mean overriding their explicit wishes? Character is what you do in the dark.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Does doing the right thing still matter if nobody sees it? What is the difference between using information strategically and using it unethically?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: School leader alone in office at night, two folders on desk representing two dilemmas, shadows symbolizing moral weight, window showing dark sky, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. Protect Priya + Take the High Road
choices.description: Override Priya's request and set up a discreet anti-bullying intervention. Destroy the information about the protesting parent's child. Refuse to weaponize private student data, ever.
choices.feedback: The highest integrity choice. You protect a vulnerable student and refuse to compromise your ethics even against those who are trying to bring you down. This is character under fire.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Choosing what's right over what's easy shows moral courage.
skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.

choices.label: B. Respect Priya's Wishes + Take the High Road
choices.description: Honor Priya's request for non-intervention but quietly check in on her regularly. Destroy the information about the protesting parent's child. Find other ways to support Priya without direct confrontation.
choices.feedback: A respectful choice that honors Priya's autonomy while maintaining your own integrity. But if the bullying escalates, you may regret not intervening sooner.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Considering fairness in your decision demonstrates ethical thinking.
skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Resisting the quick fix in favor of lasting results shows maturity.

choices.label: C. Use the Information Strategically
choices.description: Leak the connection between the protesting parent and the misinformation to a trusted ally, who can 'discover' it independently. It is true information, after all. Help Priya by giving the bullies a warning through their teachers.
choices.feedback: Effective but ethically corrosive. The protest group is discredited, and no one knows it was you. But you have crossed a line — using confidential student data as a weapon. Mr. Anand senses something has changed.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Stepping outside your comfort zone builds risk assessment skills.

choices.label: D. Seek Counsel from Principal Torres and Mr. Anand
choices.description: These dilemmas are too heavy for one person. Bring both situations (anonymized) to Principal Torres and Mr. Anand. Share the burden, get wisdom, and decide together.
choices.feedback: Wise and humble. Seeking counsel shows self-awareness and maturity. Mr. Anand offers a perspective you hadn't considered. Principal Torres helps protect Priya through official channels. The burden is shared.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Weighing the ethical implications shows principled reasoning.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.

rounds.round_title: Week 9: The Long Road to Recovery
rounds.situation: The immediate crises are managed, but the school is far from recovered. Half-repaired buildings, exhausted teachers, anxious students, and a community still divided. You have to decide what 'recovery' actually means. Is it returning to how things were before? Or is this an opportunity to build something better? A progressive education consultancy offers pro-bono help to redesign the school's approach — but it would mean big changes that not everyone wants.
rounds.goal: Define your vision for recovery and decide whether to restore or transform.
rounds.coaching_moment: Crisis creates opportunity — but only if you have the courage and energy to seize it. The temptation after a long battle is to return to normal. But 'normal' is what left the school vulnerable in the first place.
rounds.reflection_prompt: Is 'going back to normal' ever the right goal after a crisis? When does recovery become transformation?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Half-repaired school building, one side old and damaged, other side being rebuilt with modern sustainable design, workers and students together, sunrise symbolizing new beginning, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. Restore and Stabilize
choices.description: Focus on getting everything back to how it was. Fix the buildings, resume normal classes, re-establish routines. The community needs normalcy and predictability after weeks of chaos.
choices.feedback: Safe, steady, and comforting. Students and teachers breathe easier as routines return. But an opportunity for meaningful change slips away.

skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.
skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Waiting for the right moment instead of rushing shows self-control.

choices.label: B. Accept the Consultancy — Transform the School
choices.description: Use this crisis as a catalyst. Accept the pro-bono consultancy. Redesign the curriculum to include crisis management, ethics, and community service. Rebuild the gym as a multi-use community space. Go beyond recovery.
choices.feedback: Visionary and bold. The transformation plan excites some and terrifies others. Change-resistant teachers push back, but students are energized by the new possibilities.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.
skill_explanation.risk_tolerance: Being willing to try something uncertain develops risk tolerance.

choices.label: C. Student-Led Recovery Design
choices.description: Give students a genuine voice in deciding what the 'new' school looks like. Run design workshops where students propose changes. Adult oversight, student vision.
choices.feedback: Empowering and democratic. Students propose surprisingly practical and creative ideas. The process itself becomes a healing experience. But some adults feel marginalized.

skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Flexibility in your thinking helps you handle change effectively.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Standing by your values even under pressure builds integrity.

choices.label: D. Phased Approach — Stabilize Then Transform
choices.description: First two weeks: restore normalcy and rebuild basics. Then: gradually introduce reforms based on lessons learned. Balance stability with progress. Slow but sustainable.
choices.feedback: Methodical and wise. You give people the stability they need while keeping the door open for improvement. The phased approach builds consensus rather than forcing change.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Prioritizing long-term gains over short-term comfort builds character.
skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.

rounds.situation: The school board informs you that your crisis leadership mandate ends in two weeks. You need to ensure that the recovery continues without you. Key question: who takes over? And more importantly, have you built a system that works regardless of who leads? Ms. Devi wants the role. Aarav has grown enormously and could be a student co-leader. Some parents want a professional administrator brought in from outside. Principal Torres asks for your recommendation.
rounds.goal: Plan a leadership transition that sustains the recovery after your departure.
rounds.coaching_moment: The ultimate test of a leader is what happens after they leave. Do they build systems and develop people? Or do they create dependency? The best leaders make themselves unnecessary.
rounds.reflection_prompt: What makes a leader truly successful — what they achieve during their time, or what continues after they leave?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Handoff meeting in school conference room, young leader passing a folder to the next leader, team members watching, mix of emotions — pride, sadness, determination, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. Recommend Ms. Devi — Experience Matters
choices.description: Ms. Devi knows the school best, has 20 years of institutional knowledge, and commands respect from staff. Recommend her with a clear transition plan and documentation of everything you've done.
choices.feedback: A safe, solid choice. Ms. Devi will maintain stability and continue the recovery competently. But some of the innovative energy you built may fade under traditional leadership.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Choosing a future benefit over an immediate reward shows patience.
skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.

choices.label: B. Shared Leadership Model — Committee Continues
choices.description: Recommend that the crisis committee continues as a shared leadership body. No single person in charge. Collective decision-making built into the school's DNA.
choices.feedback: Democratic and sustainable. Shared leadership ensures no single point of failure. But committees are slow, and the next crisis may require faster decision-making than a committee can provide.

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Adjusting your approach when conditions change shows flexibility.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Thinking about what's fair for everyone involved shows ethical awareness.

choices.label: C. Mentor Aarav as Student Co-Leader
choices.description: Recommend Ms. Devi as official lead but with Aarav as student co-leader — a new model. Spend your remaining time mentoring Aarav in crisis management, ethics, and leadership. Build the next generation.
choices.feedback: The mentorship choice. By investing in Aarav, you ensure the school has both experience (Ms. Devi) and innovation (Aarav). This is how leaders build legacies — by developing other leaders.

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Looking beyond the obvious choice shows you think strategically.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Investing effort now for later payoff builds discipline.

choices.label: D. Build Systems, Not Dependencies
choices.description: Rather than recommending a person, create comprehensive crisis playbooks, decision frameworks, and communication templates. Make the system leader-proof. Anyone should be able to pick up where you left off.
choices.feedback: Systematic and forward-thinking. Your playbooks become the school's institutional memory. But systems without passionate people to run them can become bureaucratic and lifeless.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Planning your approach carefully is a sign of strategic reasoning.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Resisting the quick fix in favor of lasting results shows maturity.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Being open to new information and changing course builds adaptability.

rounds.situation: With one week left, you find yourself alone in the school's damaged library. The shelves are half-empty from water damage, but sunlight streams through the windows. You pull out your crisis journal and read your entries from Week 1. The person who wrote those words feels like a stranger — younger, more uncertain, but also more idealistic. Mr. Anand finds you there. 'What have you learned about yourself?' he asks. 'Not about the crisis. About YOU.'
rounds.goal: Honestly reflect on your leadership journey and what you have become.
rounds.coaching_moment: Self-reflection is the meta-skill that makes all other skills grow. Leaders who never examine their own decisions are doomed to repeat their mistakes. This is about emotional intelligence — knowing yourself.
rounds.reflection_prompt: How have you changed since Week 1? What surprised you about yourself? What would you do differently?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: Young person sitting in damaged library with journal, sunlight through broken window, bookshelves partially empty, wise elder standing in doorway watching, contemplative mood, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. 'I Learned That I Don't Have All the Answers'
choices.description: Share your biggest mistakes openly. Acknowledge the times you were wrong, the choices that backfired, the moments when others' advice was better than your instincts. True humility.
choices.feedback: Mr. Anand smiles. 'The wise person knows they are foolish. That's the beginning of real wisdom.' Your honesty inspires others to share their own reflections, creating a culture of learning.

skill_explanation.empathy: Considering how others feel shows emotional intelligence.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Choosing what's right over what's easy shows moral courage.
skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.

choices.label: B. 'I Discovered Strengths I Didn't Know I Had'
choices.description: Reflect on how the crisis brought out capabilities you never knew existed — the ability to stay calm under fire, to inspire exhausted teams, to make impossible choices and live with them.
choices.feedback: Mr. Anand nods. 'A diamond is just a lump of coal that handled pressure well.' Your self-awareness about your growth inspires others to see their own potential.

skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Pivoting your strategy when needed is a sign of adaptive thinking.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Thinking ahead about consequences shows strategic planning ability.

choices.label: C. 'I Learned What I'm NOT Willing to Compromise'
choices.description: Reflect on the ethical dilemmas. Share the moments when you were tempted to cut corners, to use information unethically, to sacrifice integrity for results. Articulate the values that held you together.
choices.feedback: Mr. Anand's eyes light up. 'THAT is leadership. Not the decisions you made, but the principles behind them.' Your moral clarity becomes a story that gets retold in the community for years.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Considering fairness in your decision demonstrates ethical thinking.
skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.
skill_explanation.empathy: Taking others' perspectives into account builds empathy.

choices.label: D. 'I Learned That Leadership Is About People, Not Problems'
choices.description: Reflect on the relationships — Ms. Devi's quiet strength, Aarav's fearless creativity, Mr. Rahman's surprising vulnerability, the displaced families' resilience. The crisis was about problems, but the solution was always about people.
choices.feedback: Mr. Anand embraces you. 'You understand something most adults never learn. A school is not a building. It is the people inside it.' Your relational leadership has transformed the community.

skill_explanation.empathy: Understanding the impact on people around you shows care for others.
skill_explanation.adaptability: Responding to unexpected situations with creativity shows adaptability.
skill_explanation.resilience: Facing challenges head-on strengthens your resilience over time.

rounds.situation: Your final day. The school holds a special assembly. Students have made a mural depicting the 12-week journey. Teachers present a bound copy of the crisis journal as a keepsake. Parents who once protested against you now stand with those who supported you. Riya Kapoor is there — not as a reporter, but as someone who was moved by what she witnessed. Principal Torres asks you to give a final address. What will you say?
rounds.goal: Deliver your final message — the legacy you want to leave behind.
rounds.coaching_moment: Legacy is not about what people remember you for — it is about what continues to grow after you are gone. Your final words are not for you. They are for the people who will carry the school forward without you.
rounds.reflection_prompt: If you could leave behind just one idea for this community, what would it be?
rounds.ai_image_prompt: School assembly hall, young leader at podium, colorful student mural in background depicting crisis and recovery, audience of students teachers parents, emotional atmosphere, sunlight through windows, semi-realistic

choices.label: A. 'Integrity Is the Only Thing Nobody Can Take from You'
choices.description: Deliver a speech about ethical leadership. Share the moments when integrity was tested and why it mattered. Challenge the community to hold future leaders — and themselves — to the same standard.
choices.feedback: The hall is silent, then erupts. Your words about integrity in crisis become the school's unofficial motto. Years later, students who were there will quote this speech.

skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Weighing the ethical implications shows principled reasoning.
skill_explanation.resilience: Pushing through difficulty builds mental strength.
skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Considering long-term impact before acting builds strategic thinking.

choices.label: B. 'We Survived Because We Had Each Other'
choices.description: Make it about the community, not yourself. Name every person who contributed — from the principal to the youngest student helper. Celebrate the collective, not the leader.
choices.feedback: People weep openly. By making others the heroes, you become the most admired leader in the school's history. The community bonds forged during the crisis become the school's greatest strength.

skill_explanation.empathy: Listening to different viewpoints strengthens your empathy skills.
skill_explanation.resilience: Choosing to persist when things get hard develops resilience.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Standing by your values even under pressure builds integrity.

choices.label: C. 'The Next Crisis Will Come — Be Ready'
choices.description: Deliver a forward-looking speech. Share the crisis playbooks, the decision frameworks, the communication templates. Make the school crisis-resilient. 'Don't remember me — prepare for what comes next.'
choices.feedback: Practical and visionary. Some are moved, some want more emotional closure, but the message is powerful: preparedness is the greatest gift a leader can leave behind.

skill_explanation.strategic_thinking: Weighing multiple outcomes before deciding strengthens your planning skills.
skill_explanation.resilience: Learning from setbacks rather than giving up shows resilience.
skill_explanation.delayed_gratification: Waiting for the right moment instead of rushing shows self-control.

choices.label: D. 'Thank You for Letting Me Lead — and for Leading Me'
choices.description: Keep it short and personal. Thank Principal Torres, Mr. Anand, Ms. Devi, Aarav, and the students individually. Acknowledge that you were changed by them more than they were changed by you. End with a simple bow.
choices.feedback: The simplest speech, and the most powerful. By thanking others, you reveal the rarest leadership quality of all: genuine humility. Mr. Anand whispers to Principal Torres, 'This one will change the world.'

skill_explanation.empathy: Valuing others' experiences alongside your own shows empathetic thinking.
skill_explanation.ethical_reasoning: Thinking about what's fair for everyone involved shows ethical awareness.
skill_explanation.resilience: Staying focused under pressure builds your ability to bounce back.

glossary_terms.definition: The process of preparing for, responding to, and recovering from unexpected, disruptive events that threaten an organization or community.
A situation where you must choose between two or more morally valid but conflicting options, where every choice carries a cost.
Any person or group who is affected by or has an interest in the decisions and actions of an organization — including students, parents, staff, and community members.
Operating in a way that is open, honest, and visible to all stakeholders, especially during difficult situations.
The capacity to recover quickly from difficulties and adapt to adversity, emerging stronger than before.
The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles, especially when no one is watching or when it is costly.
False or misleading information that is spread, whether intentionally or not, and can cause harm to individuals or communities.
The process of transferring authority, knowledge, and responsibility from one leader to the next in a way that ensures continuity.

endings.title: Crisis Commander
endings.message: You emerged as a legendary crisis leader. When the storm broke, you did not flinch. When ethics were tested, you held the line. When the community fractured, you held it together. Your crisis response became a national case study, and schools across the country now use the 'Crisis Commander Framework' you developed. Principal Torres recommends you for the National Youth Leadership Award. Your legacy: proving that a young person can lead through the worst and come out the other side not just surviving, but transformed. Every skill you learned across three years came together in this moment — and you rose to the occasion magnificently.

endings.title: Ethical Guardian
endings.message: Through every temptation, every shortcut, every moment when the easy path was unethical — you chose integrity. The community watched a young leader refuse to compromise their principles even under extreme pressure. Mr. Anand tells anyone who will listen: 'I have seen the future of leadership, and it has a moral compass.' Riya Kapoor writes a profile titled 'The Student Who Chose Integrity Over Victory' that goes viral. Your legacy is not what you built, but what you refused to break.

endings.title: Community Builder
endings.message: The buildings may still show cracks, but the community has never been stronger. You understood something fundamental: a school is not walls and roofs — it is the bonds between people. The parents who once protested against you now volunteer weekly. The teachers who were ready to quit have renewed their commitment. The students have formed peer support groups that continue long after the crisis. Your legacy: a community that knows it can survive anything, because it learned to rely on each other.

endings.title: Resilient Leader
endings.message: You bent but never broke. When crises compounded, when the media attacked, when your own team doubted you — you kept going. Not with blind stubbornness, but with the quiet strength that comes from genuine emotional resilience. Your team drew strength from your composure. Students told Principal Torres: 'When things got scary, we looked at our leader and felt okay.' Your legacy: showing that resilience is not about being tough — it is about being steady, adaptive, and genuinely strong from the inside out.

endings.title: Innovation Pioneer
endings.message: Where others saw destruction, you saw possibility. Your innovative approach to crisis communication, student empowerment, and community rebuilding became a model for schools everywhere. The digital coordination system Aarav built under your guidance is now an open-source toolkit used by schools nationwide. The education consultancy that offered pro-bono help wrote a case study calling your approach 'the most creative crisis response we have ever witnessed in a school setting.' Your legacy: turning catastrophe into catalyst.

endings.title: Growing Leader
endings.message: The crisis was bigger than anything you had ever faced, and the truth is — you struggled. Some decisions worked, others did not. Some relationships strengthened, others frayed. The recovery is incomplete and the road ahead is long. But here is what matters: you showed up. Every single day, you showed up and tried. Mr. Anand finds you after the assembly and says, 'You did not conquer the crisis — but the crisis did not conquer you either. And that, young one, is the beginning of real leadership.' This is not the end of your story. It is the foundation for everything that comes next.
